newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia appoints new U.S. ambassador.
newsitem.headline: Australia appoints new U.S. ambassador.

text.p: Australia announced on Friday the appointment of former liberal opposition leader and foreign minister Andrew Peacock as ambassador to the United States.
Peacock will replace John McCarthy early next year, when McCarthy takes up his appointment as ambassador to Indonesia.
"The government attaches very great importance to Australia's relationship with the United States," Prime Minister John Howard said in a statement.
"Our relationship is a vital one that brings immense economic and strategic benefits to both countries and to our region as a whole," he said.
Peacock served as foreign minister from 1975 to 1980 and was Australian opposition leader from 1983 to 1985 and 1989 to 1990.
Since then, he has served as a company director.
"I think my long period as foreign minister and particularly my wide range of contacts in the Congress ... will be helpful," Peacock said in a radio interview.
"We have to be very active and vigilant in seeing that legislation that is put through does not adversely impact on us," he said.
